behaviors.behavior: A suspicious Unicode codepoint quoted inside a fenced code block (``` ... ```) is not flagged
A suspicious Unicode codepoint quoted inside an inline backtick span is not flagged
A suspicious Unicode codepoint sitting in bare prose (the real hiding case) is still flagged — the fix must not blind real detection
Pre-existing detection of a hidden zero-width-joiner in bare prose (malicious_skill.md fixture) still fires after the fix
The original reported false positive (.shipwright/planning/iterate/iterate-2026-07-28-codescanning-alerts.md:63, U+202E inside an inline code span) no longer produces a finding
behaviors.evidence: Manual re-scan: scan_markdown() on the real file returns 0 findings (was 1 high before the fix); full-repo --full scan confirms only 1 unrelated pre-existing finding remains (PY_DYNAMIC_IMPORT in shared/tests/test_iterate_timing_cli.py, out of scope)

behaviors.behavior: Base64-blob detection (the sibling check reusing the same in_fence pattern) is unaffected by the Unicode-scan change

surface_verification.detail: Scanner's own test suite driven via the real pytest CLI (not mocked); includes the 3 new regression tests (fenced-block-ignored, inline-span-ignored, prose-still-flagged) plus the fixture-based malicious_skill.md unicode-detection test proving the real detection path survives the fix. Also manually verified: re-scanning the actual file that produced the original triage false positive (.shipwright/planning/iterate/iterate-2026-07-28-codescanning-alerts.md) now returns 0 findings.
